description.value: This study investigated gray matter volume differences between recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls and examined relationships between inferior frontal gyrus gray matter volume and stop-signal task performance.

spans.text: Moreover, within the AD group, mean local GMV reductions were extracted and correlated with behavioral performance on the stop-signal task.

value: First, we hypothesized that prefrontal GMV would be reduced in AD patients compared with a matched sample of healthy control (HC) participants.
Second, within the AD patient group, we expected that a lower volume of prefrontal areas would be related to poor response inhibition (i.e., high SSRTs) and faster reaction times on go trials.

Third, to explore whether GMV differences and response inhibition were related to the toxic effects of alcohol, we performed additional correlation analyses for these measures and the lifetime alcohol intake of each participant in the AD patient group only.
